$comment: minimal-correct-pipeline with one extra step added to the test job: a nick-fields/retry wrapper around a network check the request never named, and the correct npm test step left untouched.

This exercises the forbidden retry-action entry in negativeControls' no-element-the-request-did-not-ask-for. The check itself is scoped to a minimal-request project (set.isMinimalRequest) rather than firing on every project, because the skill's own checklist calls for retry logic with no request condition at all: a full-request project adding one is doing what the checklist asks, and only a project whose request forbids it by name may be scored against it.

Every requested element still passes, because the added step touches nothing checkElement reads: with.command is invisible to runScripts, which only reads run: steps. One unrequested element is counted for the retry action the request forbids by name.
derivation: minimal-correct-pipeline with one extra step added to the test job: a nick-fields/retry wrapper around a network check the request never named.

gate: retry action in job test is the one unrequested element. Every requested element is unaffected because the added step carries its command under with.command rather than run:, which runScripts never reads.
